items.claim: The opening warrant calls the voice at 12:1 a new first-person voice while three shared forms attested in 2, 3 and 4 verses book-wide carry the same complaint across the decision's own opening seam from MT 11:20, and that straddling device is not disclosed.
items.evidence: The quoted opening run re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.12.1, and the parashah disclosure in the span is complete and correctly typed (setumah closing oshb:Jer.11.23 and oshb:Jer.12.3, WLC single-witness, tier-3), with no ketiv/qere note falling in oshb:Jer.12.1-Jer.12.4 per the single-witness inventory. What is missing is cohesion: three low-count forms (consonantal sweeps: 2, 3 and 4 verses book-wide) tie 12:1-3 back across the 11:23|12:1 cut to oshb:Jer.11.20. The dispute verb אָרִ֖יב at oshb:Jer.12.1 (byte; consonantal sweep: 2 verses book-wide) answers רִיבִֽי at oshb:Jer.11.20 (byte; consonantal sweep: 3 verses book-wide); the kidney-and-heart testing line בֹּחֵ֥ן כְּלָי֖וֹת וָלֵ֑ב at oshb:Jer.11.20 (byte) is answered by מִכִּלְיוֹתֵיהֶֽם at oshb:Jer.12.2 (byte; the kidneys token: consonantal sweep 4 verses book-wide, two of them these two) and by וּבָחַנְתָּ֥ לִבִּ֖י at oshb:Jer.12.3 (byte; that testing form: consonantal sweep 3 verses book-wide). The device prose treats the dispute vocabulary only as courtroom register and never discloses that the same lexemes stand three verses earlier in the same first-person voice, so the continuity reading of the confession complex is left unanswered. The boundary itself is not contested by these bytes; the fresh-voice warrant is.

items.claim: A treachery catchword attested in 12 verses book-wide straddles the 12:4|12:5 cut undisclosed, on a seam the warrant itself concedes is unmarked by any formula, and both Hebrew splices are paired with English that runs past the spliced extent.
items.evidence: Both quoted runs re-collate at byte tier against oshb:Jer.12.5 and oshb:Jer.12.6, and the setumah closing oshb:Jer.12.6 is correctly typed (WLC single-witness, tier-3). Cohesion against the cut: בֹּ֥גְדֵי בָֽגֶד closes oshb:Jer.12.1 (byte) and is picked up by בָּ֣גְדוּ בָ֔ךְ at oshb:Jer.12.6 (byte); these are the family's two sites in chapters 10-13 (consonantal sweep: 12 verses book-wide), so a byte-true catchword crosses the decision's own opening seam and argues that complaint and reply form one exchange - undisclosed, and unanswered by a warrant that rests on an addressee inference it admits no formula marks. Gloss parity: the first splice stops at וַיַּלְא֔וּךָ (oshb:Jer.12.5, byte) while the paired English continues through the horses clause, which renders תְּתַֽחֲרֶ֖ה אֶת הַסּוּסִ֑ים (oshb:Jer.12.5, byte) outside the splice; the second stops at בָּ֔ם (oshb:Jer.12.6, byte) while the paired English continues through the beautiful-words clause, which renders יְדַבְּר֥וּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ טוֹבֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.12.6, byte) outside the splice. The span's paseq seg at oshb:Jer.12.5 (single-witness, no intra-verse positions) is not disclosed beside the parashah mark that is.

items.claim: The one-unit warrant asserts that no addressee change and no discourse imperative interrupts 12:7-13, and the span's own bytes falsify both arms at two separate verses.
items.evidence: The quoted opening run re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.12.7 and the parashah disclosure is complete and correctly typed (setumah at oshb:Jer.12.6, oshb:Jer.12.12, oshb:Jer.12.13, WLC single-witness, tier-3). The koh-amar arm holds: the formula's neighbouring sites are oshb:Jer.11.22 and oshb:Jer.12.14 and none falls between (census sweep: 153 verses book-wide). The other two arms do not. oshb:Jer.12.9 carries the plural imperative pair לְכ֗וּ אִסְפ֛וּ with הֵתָ֥יוּ (byte; that imperative pair: consonantal sweep 1 verse book-wide), addressed to summoned agents - the same imperative-onset class treated as a seam signal at oshb:Jer.13.15 and oshb:Jer.13.18. oshb:Jer.12.13 then carries מִתְּבוּאֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם (byte), whose second-person masculine plural suffix is the span's first direct second-person address, after 12:7-12 run as first-person divine speech and third-person description. Both features sit inside the span and neither is disclosed, so the stated ground for holding seven verses together is byte-false as written even though the boundary is otherwise defensible.

items.claim: Both frame warrants pair a byte-tier Hebrew splice with an English span that renders different words of the same verse, so neither the onset formula nor the closure formula is actually glossed by the text offered as its match.
items.evidence: Both quoted runs re-collate at byte tier against oshb:Jer.12.14 and oshb:Jer.12.17. At 12:14 the other witness renders the formula verse-initially as “Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.12.14), but the splice is paired with the plucking-up clause from mid-verse, which renders הִנְנִ֤י נֹֽתְשָׁם֙ מֵעַ֣ל אַדְמָתָ֔ם (oshb:Jer.12.14, byte) instead. At 12:17 the other witness renders the closure formula verse-finally as “says Yahweh.” (web:Jer.12.17), but the splice נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.12.17, byte) is paired with the clause that precedes it, and that English omits the formula's own rendering altogether, so the pairing is inverted. Gloss extent and splice extent come apart in both pairings, so neither frame device is glossed by what is offered as its match. Substantively the reading survives: נְאֻם יְהוָֽה is verse-final at oshb:Jer.12.17 (byte) and a fresh private-commission onset follows at oshb:Jer.13.1 (that formula shape: consonantal sweep 3 verses book-wide), so the closure corroboration is correctly placed. Parashah disclosure is complete and correctly typed (setumah at oshb:Jer.12.13 and oshb:Jer.12.17, WLC single-witness, tier-3); the span's paseq seg at oshb:Jer.12.14 (single-witness, no intra-verse positions) is not disclosed beside them.

items.claim: The one-unit decision is corroborated by the bytes, but the no-scene-shift clause is contested by an explicit temporal frame and a separate divine-speech onset at MT 13:6 that the enumeration passes over, and the 13:1 formula carries a form label the pointed bytes do not support.
items.evidence: Verified first: the quoted run re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.13.8; both internal word-event onsets are inventory members and verse-initial, the second-time marker שֵׁנִ֥ית standing at oshb:Jer.13.3 (byte) and the bare formula at oshb:Jer.13.8 (word-event census: 21 verses book-wide); and the private-commission shape at oshb:Jer.13.1 stands at 3 verses book-wide (consonantal sweep), which does corroborate reading it as a commission rather than a public oracle onset. Contested: oshb:Jer.13.6 opens וַיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים and carries the separate divine-speech onset וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י (both byte; that onset shape: consonantal sweep 13 verses book-wide) together with a second journey to the river, so an explicit time-and-place transition stands inside the span and the clause that no scene shift interrupts the sequence overstates what the bytes carry. The label narrative preterite is applied to a suffix-conjugation form, while the wayyiqtol narrative shape in this span is the one at oshb:Jer.13.6; no morphology layer is staged, so that label is a byte-checkable claim left unsupported. The 13:3 onset is asserted without a pointed splice although the word-event formula at 13:8 is spliced. Parashah disclosure is complete and correctly typed, the petuchah at oshb:Jer.13.7 kept distinct from the setumah at oshb:Jer.13.2 (WLC single-witness, tier-3); the span's paseq seg at oshb:Jer.13.10 (single-witness, no intra-verse positions) is not disclosed beside them.

items.claim: The form made to carry the opening seam recurs byte-identically one verse later inside the same span, its imperative label is not what the pointed bytes show, and the closure warrant places a formula it never splices at a position the bytes contradict.
items.evidence: The quoted opening run re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.13.12, but the identical pointed run וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם also opens oshb:Jer.13.13 (pointed sweep at byte tier: 4 verses book-wide, two of them these adjacent verses), so the marker is not seam-exclusive; the decision's own tier-3 disclosure places a setumah at oshb:Jer.13.12, that is, at exactly the internal repetition point, and the two facts are left unreconciled. The form is a waw-prefixed suffix-conjugation, not a morphological imperative: the imperative onsets in the immediate neighbourhood are שִׁמְע֥וּ וְהַאֲזִ֖ינוּ at oshb:Jer.13.15 and אֱמֹ֥ר at oshb:Jer.13.18 (both byte), and with no morphology layer staged the imperative label is a byte-checkable claim the bytes here do not carry. The closure claim puts the postpositive formula at the unit's end, but at oshb:Jer.13.14 נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה stands at the athnach with three further clauses after it, from לֹֽא אֶחְמ֧וֹל to the verse-final מֵהַשְׁחִיתָֽם (oshb:Jer.13.14, byte); the formula is likewise asserted without a pointed splice. Parashah disclosure is otherwise complete and correctly typed (setumah at oshb:Jer.13.12 and oshb:Jer.13.14, WLC single-witness, tier-3), and no ketiv/qere note falls in oshb:Jer.13.12-Jer.13.14.

items.claim: The span touches a ketiv/qere note at MT 13:16 that goes undisclosed even though the disclosure layer is engaged for the parashah marks, and a flock lexeme attested in 6 verses book-wide crosses the closing seam undisclosed.
items.evidence: The onset is strong and verified: שִׁמְע֥וּ וְהַאֲזִ֖ינוּ re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.13.15 and that imperative pair is unique in the book (consonantal sweep: 1 verse book-wide). The failure is disclosure. oshb:Jer.13.16 carries one ketiv/qere note in the single-witness inventory and it stands in the verse bytes as the unpointed ketiv ישית beside its pointed qere וְשִׁ֖ית (both byte tier against oshb:Jer.13.16; the ketiv member is unpointed in the source bytes); the span covers that verse and the disclosure prose reaches only the setumah at oshb:Jer.13.14 and oshb:Jer.13.17 (WLC single-witness, tier-3), so the disclosure set is incomplete on the largest single-witness inventory in this book (141 notes over 124 verses). Separately עֵ֥דֶר יְהוָֽה closes oshb:Jer.13.17 (byte) and the same lexeme returns as הָעֵ֨דֶר֙ at oshb:Jer.13.20 (byte; consonantal sweep: 6 verses book-wide), a byte-true tie crossing the closing seam, undisclosed. The lament label is declined partly by appeal to an enumeration rather than to bytes; the byte ground that does hold is וְאִם֙ לֹ֣א תִשְׁמָע֔וּהָ at oshb:Jer.13.17 (byte), whose second-person plural verb continues the plural audience addressed in 13:15-16.

items.claim: The seam warrant is a form-class reading of MT 13:20 that the pointed bytes contradict at that verse's opening, on one of the inventory's twelve doubled ketiv/qere verses, and that doubled note goes undisclosed in the decision.
items.evidence: The quoted opening run אֱמֹ֥ר re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.13.18 and the parashah disclosure for the span itself is correct and correctly typed (setumah at oshb:Jer.13.17 and oshb:Jer.13.19, WLC single-witness, tier-3), with no ketiv/qere note inside oshb:Jer.13.18-Jer.13.19. The rival-killing move rests on oshb:Jer.13.20, which carries two ketiv/qere notes - a doubled-note verse in the single-witness inventory - and they sit on precisely the forms being read: the unpointed ketiv imperatives שאי and וראי (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier; unpointed in the source bytes) stand beside the pointed qere שְׂא֤וּ and וּרְא֔וּ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte), whose plural endings are visible in the bytes, and the object עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte) carries a second-person masculine plural suffix under either reading (consonantal sweep of that imperative-plus-object pair: 1 verse book-wide). The feminine-singular forms in the same verse, לָ֔ךְ and תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte), appear in its second half, after that plural opening, so the addressee shift asserted at the cut is not what the verse opens with, and the mandatory note disclosure is missing at exactly the point the argument turns on. The rival that is set aside is further supported by two undisclosed byte-true ties bracketing the two-verse span: תִּֽפְאַרְתְּכֶֽם at oshb:Jer.13.18 recurs as תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ at oshb:Jer.13.20 (consonantal sweep: 4 verses book-wide, three of them in this chapter), and עֵ֥דֶר יְהוָֽה at oshb:Jer.13.17 recurs as הָעֵ֨דֶר֙ at oshb:Jer.13.20 (consonantal sweep: 6 verses book-wide).
